tracks.title: Starter
tracks.subtitle: Starting out in development
tracks.description: The basics of JavaScript and your first key skills. This is where the foundation is built, and without it you cannot move forward.

tracks.title: Junior
tracks.subtitle: Confident foundation
tracks.description: The next stage of growth: applied logic, real project structure, working with data, APIs, and interfaces.

tracks.title: Middle
tracks.subtitle: Applied development
tracks.description: Architecture, scaling, asynchrony, application structure, and a mature approach to development.

tracks.title: Senior
tracks.subtitle: Systems thinking
tracks.description: Deep platform understanding, optimization, patterns, design, and a systems-level approach to development.

tracks.title: Bonuses
tracks.subtitle: Additional materials
tracks.description: Bonus modules, extra breakdowns, useful practical blocks, and extended materials will appear here.

hero.goal: Understand how JS is connected, how to output data, and what data means in JavaScript.
hero.description: This is the foundation you cannot move forward without. The first step in JavaScript is understanding how the language gets onto the page, how to see the result of your work, and how data is structured.

modules.summary: After completing this module, you should see JavaScript as a language that works with data, variables, types, and the logic of connecting to HTML.

topics.title: Connecting JavaScript to HTML
topics.intro: Understand how JavaScript gets onto the page and exactly when it starts executing.
deepDive: why the DOM is not ready yet
difference between script, defer, and async
topics.important: JS can execute after the HTML loads or in parallel, and this affects access to the DOM.

topics.title: Debugging and data output
topics.intro: Without the console and DevTools, learning JavaScript turns into guesswork.
deepDive: how to inspect objects and arrays
topics.important: This is the foundation of debugging and a habit you will struggle without later.

topics.title: Variables
topics.intro: Variables are used to store data and work with it inside the code.
deepDive: difference between let, const, and var
why const does not make an object immutable
topics.example:
let age = 27
const name = "Bogdan"
const user = {}
user.name = "Alex"
topics.important: const prevents reassigning the reference, but it does not prevent changing the contents of an object.

topics.title: Data types
topics.intro: This is the foundation of all JavaScript.
topics.example:
let price = 10.5
const name = "Bogdan"
const isOnline = true
let user = null
let age
topics.important: The difference between null and undefined is a common question, and you need to understand it confidently.

topics.title: Checking a data type
topics.intro: You need to be able to quickly understand what type you are looking at.
deepDive: the historical quirk of typeof null
topics.example:
typeof 5
typeof "hello"
typeof true
typeof null
topics.important: typeof null returns object — this is a historical JavaScript bug.

practice.finalThought: JavaScript is a language for working with data. The first thing to understand is: data → variables → data types.

hero.goal: Understand how JavaScript compares and evaluates values.
hero.description: This module lays the foundation of logic: calculations, comparisons, strict and loose checks, logical operators, and the ternary operator.

modules.summary: After this module, you should understand how JavaScript evaluates expressions and how to use operators to make decisions in code.

topics.title: Arithmetic operators
topics.intro: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and the remainder operator.
topics.example:
let a = 10
let b = 3
console.log(a + b)
console.log(a % b)
topics.important: % is especially important for parity checks, loops, and distributing elements.

topics.title: Comparison operators
topics.intro: They compare values and return true or false.
topics.important: Strings are compared by Unicode.

topics.title: Loose comparison
topics.intro: Comparison with type coercion.
topics.important: Loose comparison often leads to bugs.

topics.title: Strict comparison
topics.intro: Checks both the value and the type.
deepDive: why it is better to use strict comparison
topics.important: A good habit is to use === and !== almost always.

topics.title: Assignment operators
topics.intro: They change a variable value and shorten the syntax.
topics.important: Short assignment operators make code more compact.

topics.title: Increment and decrement
topics.intro: They are often used in loops and when changing values step by step.
topics.important: You need to understand the difference between postfix and prefix.

topics.title: Logical operators
topics.intro: They let you combine checks.
topics.important: This is the foundation of all conditional logic.

topics.title: Nullish coalescing operator
topics.intro: Provides a default value only if the left side is null or undefined.
topics.important: ?? preserves 0, an empty string, and false.

topics.title: Optional chaining
topics.intro: Safe access to nested properties.
topics.important: If the property does not exist, no error occurs.

topics.title: Ternary operator
topics.intro: A short form of if.
deepDive: when not to use it for complex logic
topics.important: The ternary operator is good for short and readable conditions.

practice.finalThought: JavaScript is a language of conditions and logic. Operators are decision-making tools.

hero.goal: Learn to build conditions and control program behavior.
hero.description: This module teaches you to make decisions in code: if, else, else if, switch, truthy/falsy, and short conditions.

modules.summary: After completing this module, you should confidently build conditions and write cleaner, clearer logic.

topics.title: Logical operators
topics.intro: They allow you to combine conditions together.
topics.important: Logical operators often return actual values, not only true or false.

topics.title: if
topics.intro: The basic conditional construct.
topics.important: if is the foundation of any branching logic.

topics.title: else
topics.intro: Executes if the if condition turns out to be false.
topics.important: else describes alternative behavior.

topics.title: else if
topics.intro: Adds additional checks.
deepDive: conditions are evaluated from top to bottom
topics.important: The order of conditions matters.

topics.title: Ternary operator
topics.intro: A short form of if.
topics.important: Suitable only for short logic.

topics.title: switch
topics.intro: Compares one value against several options.
topics.example:
switch(day) {
 case "Monday":
   console.log("work day")
   break
 default:
   console.log("regular day")
}
topics.important: Useful when you need to compare one value with several exact options.

topics.title: Nested conditions
topics.intro: These are conditions inside other conditions.
topics.important: Try not to make logic too deeply nested.

topics.title: Short conditions
topics.intro: JavaScript allows you to write conditions compactly.
topics.example:
isAdmin && showPanel()
let name = userName || "Guest"
let name2 = userName ?? "Guest"
topics.important: Compact code should still remain readable.

topics.title: Truthy / Falsy
topics.intro: Not all values are coerced to true in the same way.
topics.important: This is one of the key topics in all JavaScript logic.

topics.title: Clean conditional logic
topics.intro: Good logic is logic that is clear and readable.
topics.important: The simpler your conditions are written, the easier the code is to maintain.

tasks: output the maximum of two numbers
determine the day of the week via switch
practice.finalThought: Programs are decision trees. JavaScript helps implement logic: if → then, otherwise → different behavior.

outcomes: build conditions with if, else, and else if
write cleaner and more readable logic

hero.goal: Learn to repeat actions programmatically instead of writing the same code many times.
hero.description: This module shows how to control repetition in JavaScript: for, while, do while, break, continue, nested loops, and iterating over arrays.

modules.summary: After completing this module, you should understand how loops work in JavaScript and how to use them consciously.

topics.title: for loop
topics.intro: The most universal loop in JavaScript.
topics.important: Each part of for has its own role: start, check, and counter update.

topics.title: Loop counter
topics.intro: A variable that controls the number of repetitions.
deepDive: whether other names can be used
topics.important: The main thing is that it is clear this variable is the loop counter.

topics.title: while loop
topics.intro: Runs while the condition is true.
deepDive: useful when the number of repetitions is unknown
topics.important: In while, you must not forget to change the variable that affects the condition.

topics.title: do while loop
topics.intro: Executes at least once.
topics.important: Suitable for scenarios where code must run at least once.

topics.title: break
topics.intro: Completely stops the loop.
topics.important: break is needed when there is no point in continuing the loop.

topics.title: continue
topics.intro: Skips one iteration.
topics.important: break ends the whole loop, while continue skips only the current step.

topics.title: Nested loops
topics.intro: A loop inside another loop.
topics.important: They are useful, but they increase the load on the algorithm.

topics.title: Iterating over an array with a loop
topics.intro: One of the most common tasks.
topics.important: arr.length is the number of elements in the array.

topics.title: Reverse loop
topics.intro: Sometimes you need to go from the end of an array.
topics.important: A reverse loop is often useful when removing elements.

topics.title: Infinite loop
topics.intro: A loop that never ends.
deepDive: a typical mistake is forgetting the counter
topics.important: One of the most common beginner mistakes is forgetting to change the exit condition.

tasks: calculate the sum of an array
find the maximum number in an array
output a 5×5 table using nested loops
practice.finalThought: Loops let you turn one instruction into thousands of actions. This is the foundation of algorithms, data processing, and interface generation.

outcomes: understand how the for loop works
iterate over arrays with a loop

hero.goal: Learn to break a program into reusable blocks of code.
hero.description: This module shows how to turn a set of commands into a clear and flexible structure using functions.

modules.summary: After completing this module, you should understand how functions help avoid code repetition and build application architecture.

topics.title: Function Declaration
topics.intro: The classic way to declare a function.
topics.important: Function Declaration can be called before its declaration thanks to hoisting.

topics.title: Function parameters
topics.intro: Functions can receive data from outside.
topics.important: Parameters are inside the declaration, arguments are the actual values passed during the call.

topics.title: return
topics.intro: A function can return the result of its work.
deepDive: after return, code no longer executes
topics.important: return ends the execution of a function.

topics.title: Function Expression
topics.intro: A function used as a variable value.
deepDive: no hoisting like Function Declaration has
topics.important: It is important to understand the moment when the variable is initialized.

topics.title: Arrow functions
topics.intro: A modern syntax for writing functions.
deepDive: arrow functions do not have their own this
topics.important: This is one of the most important features of arrow functions.

topics.title: Default parameters
topics.intro: You can set a value if an argument is not passed.
topics.important: This helps make functions more reliable.

topics.title: Rest parameters
topics.intro: Allow you to accept any number of arguments.
deepDive: rest is always the last parameter
topics.important: Rest collects arguments into an array.

topics.title: Spread operator
topics.intro: Expands an array or an object.
topics.important: One syntax, but two different meanings: rest and spread.

topics.title: Scope
topics.intro: Defines where a variable is accessible.
topics.important: Scope is the foundation for understanding code structure.

topics.title: Closure
topics.intro: A function remembers variables from its outer environment.
deepDive: why the inner function remembers count
topics.important: Closures are one of the most powerful concepts in JavaScript.

tasks: create a function that adds numbers
create a function that finds the maximum number
create a function that takes an array and returns the sum
create a function with a default value
create a simple counter using closure
practice.finalThought: Functions allow you to write small programs inside a program. Libraries, frameworks, and application architecture are built through functions.

hero.goal: Learn to store and modify a set of data.
hero.description: This module introduces arrays, one of the most important data structures in JavaScript.

modules.summary: After completing this module, you should understand how arrays help store lists of data and how to change their contents.

topics.title: Creating an array
topics.intro: An array is an ordered list of values.
topics.example:
let arr = [1,2,3]
let data = [10, "hello", true, null]
topics.important: Technically, an array is an object, but it is used as a list of values.

topics.title: Access by index
topics.intro: Each element has an index that starts from 0.
topics.important: arr.length is the number of elements in the array.

topics.title: push
topics.intro: Adds an element to the end of an array.
topics.important: push mutates the original array.

topics.title: pop
topics.intro: Removes the last element of an array.
topics.important: pop returns the removed element itself.

topics.title: shift
topics.intro: Removes the first element of an array.
topics.important: After shift, all remaining elements are moved.

topics.title: unshift
topics.intro: Adds an element to the beginning of an array.
topics.important: It works with the beginning of the array, not the end.

topics.title: slice
topics.intro: Creates a copy of part of an array.
deepDive: does not change the original array
topics.important: slice returns a new array.

topics.title: splice
topics.intro: The most powerful method for changing an array.
topics.important: slice and splice are easy to confuse, but splice mutates the array.

topics.title: concat
topics.intro: Combines arrays.
deepDive: does not change the original arrays
topics.important: concat creates a new array.

topics.title: includes
topics.intro: Checks whether an element exists.
topics.important: It is useful for logical checks.

tasks: add an element to the end of the array
create a copy of part of an array
check if an element exists using includes
practice.finalThought: An array is a structure that lets you store, iterate, modify, and process data.

outcomes: understand which methods change an array and which create a new one

hero.goal: Learn to process arrays declaratively instead of using loops.
hero.description: Strong JS code often looks like a chain of array methods: filter, map, reduce, and others.

modules.summary: After this module, you should understand how to process arrays using the modern declarative approach.

topics.title: forEach
topics.intro: The simplest method for iterating over an array.
topics.important: forEach is needed when you want to perform an action, not get a new array.

topics.title: map
topics.intro: Creates a new array.
deepDive: does not change the original array
topics.example:
let numbers = [1,2,3]
let result = numbers.map(n => n * 2)
topics.important: map is one of the most important methods in modern JavaScript.

topics.title: filter
topics.intro: Keeps only the elements that pass the condition.
topics.example:
let numbers = [1,2,3,4]
let result = numbers.filter(n => n > 2)
topics.important: filter creates a new array containing only the required elements.

topics.title: reduce
topics.intro: Lets you turn an array into a single value.
topics.example:
let numbers = [1,2,3]
let sum = numbers.reduce((acc, n) => acc + n, 0)
topics.important: reduce is the most powerful array method.

topics.title: find
topics.intro: Finds the first element that matches the condition.
deepDive: returns an element, not an array
topics.important: If you need only the first matching element, use find.

topics.title: some
topics.intro: Checks whether there is at least one matching element.
topics.important: some answers the question: does at least one such element exist?

topics.title: every
topics.intro: Checks whether all elements satisfy the condition.
topics.important: every checks the condition for the entire array.

topics.title: sort
topics.intro: Sorts an array.
deepDive: by default it sorts as strings
topics.important: A callback is required to sort numbers correctly.

topics.title: reverse
topics.intro: Reverses an array.
topics.important: reverse mutates the original array.

topics.title: flat
topics.intro: Flattens nested arrays.
topics.important: Useful when data comes nested.

tasks: double an array of numbers using map
keep only even numbers using filter
check whether there are negative numbers
practice.finalThought: Array methods let you write code in the style of: data → processing → result. This is the style of modern JavaScript.

hero.goal: Learn to create and manage structured data.
hero.description: Objects let you store data by keys and structure information in a convenient way.

modules.summary: After completing this module, you should understand how to create objects, work with properties, and iterate over object data.

topics.title: Creating an object
topics.intro: An object is created with curly braces.
deepDive: keys in an object are strings
topics.important: An object is a structure for storing related data.

topics.title: Object properties
topics.intro: Each key of an object is one of its properties.
deepDive: properties describe the characteristics of an object
topics.important: Properties are a way to describe an entity.

topics.title: Dot notation
topics.intro: The most common way to work with properties.
deepDive: works when the key is known in advance
topics.important: Dot notation is the most convenient when the key is known.

topics.title: Bracket notation
topics.intro: Needed when the property name is stored in a variable.
topics.important: [] is needed for dynamic access.

topics.title: Adding a property
topics.intro: An object can be changed after it is created.
topics.important: New properties can be added at any time.

topics.title: Deleting a property
topics.intro: delete is used to remove a property.
topics.important: delete mutates the original object.

topics.title: this
topics.intro: The context of the current object.
deepDive: this depends on the way a function is called
arrow functions do not have their own this
topics.important: this is one of the most important topics in working with objects.

topics.title: Object.keys
topics.intro: Returns an array of an object's keys.
topics.important: Useful when you need to get all keys.

topics.title: Object.values
topics.intro: Returns an array of an object's values.
topics.important: Convenient when you need only the values.

topics.title: Object.entries
topics.intro: Returns key-value pairs.
deepDive: very useful for iterating over an object
topics.important: Lets you conveniently work with both the key and the value.

practice.finalThought: Objects let you structure data. This is the foundation of APIs, applications, and code architecture.

outcomes: distinguish dot notation and bracket notation

hero.goal: Learn to find HTML elements and change them with JavaScript.
hero.description: The DOM is the structure of an HTML page represented as a tree of objects that JavaScript works with.

modules.summary: After completing this module, you should understand how JavaScript gets access to HTML and changes elements on the page.

topics.title: document
topics.intro: The main point of access to the page.
deepDive: the DOM is the object model of HTML
topics.important: All work with the DOM starts through document.

topics.title: querySelector
topics.intro: Finds the first element by a CSS selector.
topics.important: One of the most universal ways to find an element.

topics.title: querySelectorAll
topics.intro: Finds all elements by a selector.
deepDive: NodeList looks like an array, but it is not an array
topics.important: Needed when you work with a group of elements.

topics.title: getElementById
topics.intro: The fastest way to find an element by id.
topics.important: If there is an id, this is a very convenient method.

topics.title: textContent
topics.intro: Reads and changes the text of an element.
topics.important: textContent inserts text, not HTML.

topics.title: innerHTML
topics.intro: Lets you insert HTML code.
topics.important: innerHTML should be used carefully.

topics.title: classList
topics.intro: Lets you work with classes.
deepDive: the main way to control styles through JS
topics.important: classList is a key tool for interface control.

topics.title: setAttribute
topics.intro: Adds or changes an attribute.
topics.important: Convenient for universal work with attributes.

topics.title: removeAttribute
topics.intro: Removes an attribute from an element.
deepDive: returning an element to its normal state
topics.important: Often used in forms and interactive interfaces.

topics.title: dataset
topics.intro: Working with data attributes.
topics.important: Very convenient for passing data to interface elements.

practice.finalThought: The DOM lets JavaScript control HTML. This is how a page becomes interactive.

hero.goal: Learn to create, insert, and remove HTML elements with JavaScript.
hero.description: This module is dedicated to dynamic DOM control: creating, inserting, removing, and cloning elements.

modules.summary: After completing this module, you should understand how JavaScript creates HTML elements, inserts them, removes them, and controls the DOM structure.

topics.title: createElement
topics.intro: Creates a new HTML element in memory.
deepDive: 2 stages: creation and insertion into the DOM
topics.important: createElement alone does not yet insert the element into the page.

topics.title: append
topics.intro: Adds an element to the end of the parent.
deepDive: can add text, elements, and several elements
topics.important: append is one of the most convenient ways to insert an element.

topics.title: prepend
topics.intro: Adds an element to the beginning of the parent.
topics.important: Suitable when a new element should appear first.

topics.title: before
topics.intro: Inserts an element before the current element.
deepDive: positioning relative to the current node
topics.important: Convenient for precise insertion into the DOM.

topics.title: after
topics.intro: Inserts an element after the current element.
deepDive: placing it next to the current element
topics.important: Convenient when you need to insert an element immediately after another one.

topics.title: remove
topics.intro: Removes an element from the DOM.
deepDive: removed only from the DOM, the variable can remain
topics.important: The element disappears from the page, but the JS reference to it may still remain.

topics.title: cloneNode
topics.intro: Creates a copy of an element.
topics.important: Very useful for reusing a ready-made structure.

topics.title: parentNode
topics.intro: Lets you get the parent element.
topics.important: Needed when you need to reach the parent and work with it.

topics.title: children
topics.intro: Gets all children of an element.
topics.important: children returns child elements, not any kind of content.

topics.title: closest
topics.intro: Finds the nearest parent by selector.
deepDive: very convenient for events and delegation
topics.important: One of the most useful methods for interactive interfaces.

tasks: insert an element into a list
practice.finalThought: DOM Manipulation allows JavaScript to create HTML. This is the foundation of interactive interfaces, SPA applications, and UI components.

outcomes: add elements with append and prepend
insert elements with before and after
